title: CA AB1609: Customer service chatbots.

obligations: A large private business shall provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the customer service chatbot is artificially generated and not human if a reasonable person interacting with the customer service chatbot is likely to be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human (Sec. 22626(b)).
The disclosure required by subdivision (b) shall be clear and conspicuous, and provided in the medium in which the customer service chatbot interacts with the customer (Sec. 22626(c)).

During at least a large private business's regular business hours, a large private business shall provide customers who require customer assistance with goods or services offered by or provided from the large private business with a simple customer service feature on all platforms through which the large private business provides customer service, including online chatbot customer service and telephonic customer service platforms, that allows customers to request to connect to a customer service agent (Sec. 22627(a)).

A large private business shall make a good faith effort to provide a customer who requests to connect to a customer service agent through the feature described in subdivision (a) with connection to a customer service agent within 15 minutes of the request or a specific appointment time within one business day of the request at which a customer service agent will call or connect with the customer (Sec. 22627(b)(1)).

A large private business subject to Section 1707.2 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations may satisfy the requirements in paragraph (1) by returning a phone call within one business hour (Sec. 22627(b)(2)).

A large private business shall make a good faith effort to ensure a customer is not placed on hold or made to wait for more than 15 minutes at any time after connection with a customer service agent, and that cumulative hold or wait times or escalation queues do not exceed more than one hour total (Sec. 22627(c)).

Large private businesses who provide goods and services to customers in California through online platforms and who have a telephonic customer service platform shall post their telephonic customer service telephone number clearly and conspicuously on their internet website (Sec. 22627(d)).
prohibitions: A large private business shall not represent that a customer service chatbot is a human (Sec. 22626(a)).
reading.what_it_does: This chapter prohibits large private businesses from representing that a customer service chatbot is a human and requires a clear disclosure when a reasonable person would likely be misled. It requires large private businesses to provide a customer service feature to request a human agent during regular business hours and to make good faith efforts to connect within 15 minutes or schedule an appointment, with limits on hold times. It authorizes public prosecutors to enforce and imposes civil penalties, with no private right of action.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence: an engineered or machine based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments (Sec. 22625(a)).
Customer: a natural person residing in California; residence refers to the customer's account address (Sec. 22625(b)).

Customer service agent: a natural person who, as an employee, contractor, or representative of the large private business provides either direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services, or direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services (Sec. 22625(c)).

Customer service chatbot: an artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human like responses to user inputs and is used by an entity for direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale or delivery of goods or services, or direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale or delivery of goods or services (Sec. 22625(d)).

Exclusive business lines: telephone lines, chat lines, or other communications channels that are not intended for general customer use and are intended solely for use by employees of the business or by other entities for business to business communications; entities include other businesses, nonprofit entities, or government entities (Sec. 22625(e)).
Hospital: a health facility licensed pursuant to subdivision (a), (b), or (f) of Section 1250 of the Health and Safety Code (Sec. 22625(f)).
Large private business: a business with more than five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in gross annual revenue nationally that provides goods and services to customers (Sec. 22625(g)).

Online customer service platforms: large private businesses that primarily operate on public facing internet websites, web applications, or digital applications, including a social network or publication and may not offer telephonic means of communication for customer service inquiries (Sec. 22625(h)).

Regular business hours: the hours during which the business customarily maintains customer service functions, excluding on days that the business is ordinarily closed or state or federal holidays; regular business hours includes a 10 hour period per day over a five day week or 8 hours per day for a full seven day week (Sec. 22625(i)).

Services: services for which a customer will provide or has provided monetary consideration, whether through a one time payment, subscription, fee, or recurring charge; services does not include services or parts of services that offer a free option to persons with an opportunity to pay, subscribe, or otherwise provide monetary consideration for the service or upgraded services at a future time (Sec. 22625(j)).
Telephonic customer service platforms: any large private business that provides customer service to customers in California through telephonic means (Sec. 22625(k)).
compliance_steps: Determine whether the organisation qualifies as a large private business under Sec. 22625(g).
Identify all customer service chatbots and ensure they do not represent themselves as human (Sec. 22626(a)).
Implement a clear and conspicuous disclosure in the interaction medium when a reasonable person would likely be misled into believing the chatbot is human (Sec. 22626(b),(c)).
Provide a simple customer service feature on all platforms during regular business hours that allows customers to request a customer service agent (Sec. 22627(a)).

Establish procedures to connect a requesting customer to an agent within 15 minutes or schedule a specific appointment within one business day, or return a phone call within one business hour if subject to Section 1707.2 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations (Sec. 22627(b)).
Implement hold time limits so a customer is not on hold for more than 15 minutes at any time after connection and cumulative hold or wait times do not exceed one hour total (Sec. 22627(c)).

If the business provides goods and services online and has a telephonic customer service platform, post the telephonic customer service telephone number clearly and conspicuously on the internet website (Sec. 22627(d)).
Use commercially reasonable and practicable standards designed and intended to achieve compliance to satisfy the good faith effort requirements (Sec. 22628(c)).
Review the exemptions and exceptions in Sec. 22627(e) and Sec. 22628(e),(f),(g) to determine applicability.
Prepare for enforcement by public prosecutors and potential civil penalties under Sec. 22628(a),(b).
who_it_applies_to: Large private business, defined as a business with more than five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in gross annual revenue nationally that provides goods and services to customers (Sec. 22625(g)).
notable_exemptions: The 15 minute connection or response requirement does not apply if the request or connection is made via electronic mail, web based contact form, or voicemail message (Sec. 22627(e)(1)).

The chapter does not require a large private business to offer customer service through a communication platform that the business has not otherwise made available to customers as of January 1, 2027 (Sec. 22627(e)(2)).

A large private business that as of January 1, 2027 does not utilize any telephonic customer services to customers is not required to provide telephonic customer service if it offers customer service methods by which the customer may promptly connect with a customer service agent consistent with this section (Sec. 22628(e)).

A large private business's inability to comply is not a violation if due to unforeseen circumstances beyond its reasonable control or extraordinary or emergency situations, including local or statewide emergencies, grid emergencies or public safety power shutoff events, or information technology or telecommunications outages (Sec. 22628(f)).

Services a large private business provides subject to, and in compliance with, General Order 133, Rules Governing Telecommunications Services, or General Order 103-A, Rules Governing Water Service, of the Public Utilities Commission of the State of California and in compliance with a corrective action plan, if any (Sec. 22628(g)(1)).

A hospital, when its communications relate to the provision, coordination, management, administration, payment, or operation of health care services, including patient care, clinical services, appointment scheduling, intake and registration, referrals, care coordination, patient navigation, emergency services, utilization management, prior authorization, discharge planning, followup care, billing, insurance, patient financial services, or other administrative or operational functions directly related to the delivery, payment, or coordination of health care services (Sec. 22628(g)(3)).
A consumer reporting agency, as defined in the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. Sec. 1681 et seq.) (Sec. 22628(g)(4)).

What it does

This chapter prohibits large private businesses from representing that a customer service chatbot is a human and requires a clear disclosure when a reasonable person would likely be misled. It requires large private businesses to provide a customer service feature to request a human agent during regular business hours and to make good faith efforts to connect within 15 minutes or schedule an appointment, with limits on hold times. It authorizes public prosecutors to enforce and imposes civil penalties, with no private right of action.

Who it applies to

  • Large private business, defined as a business with more than five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in gross annual revenue nationally that provides goods and services to customers (Sec. 22625(g)).

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: an engineered or machine based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments (Sec. 22625(a)).
  • Customer: a natural person residing in California; residence refers to the customer's account address (Sec. 22625(b)).
  • Customer service agent: a natural person who, as an employee, contractor, or representative of the large private business provides either direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services, or direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services (Sec. 22625(c)).
  • Customer service chatbot: an artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human like responses to user inputs and is used by an entity for direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale or delivery of goods or services, or direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale or delivery of goods or services (Sec. 22625(d)).
  • Exclusive business lines: telephone lines, chat lines, or other communications channels that are not intended for general customer use and are intended solely for use by employees of the business or by other entities for business to business communications; entities include other businesses, nonprofit entities, or government entities (Sec. 22625(e)).
  • Hospital: a health facility licensed pursuant to subdivision (a), (b), or (f) of Section 1250 of the Health and Safety Code (Sec. 22625(f)).
  • Large private business: a business with more than five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in gross annual revenue nationally that provides goods and services to customers (Sec. 22625(g)).
  • Online customer service platforms: large private businesses that primarily operate on public facing internet websites, web applications, or digital applications, including a social network or publication and may not offer telephonic means of communication for customer service inquiries (Sec. 22625(h)).
  • Regular business hours: the hours during which the business customarily maintains customer service functions, excluding on days that the business is ordinarily closed or state or federal holidays; regular business hours includes a 10 hour period per day over a five day week or 8 hours per day for a full seven day week (Sec. 22625(i)).
  • Services: services for which a customer will provide or has provided monetary consideration, whether through a one time payment, subscription, fee, or recurring charge; services does not include services or parts of services that offer a free option to persons with an opportunity to pay, subscribe, or otherwise provide monetary consideration for the service or upgraded services at a future time (Sec. 22625(j)).
  • Telephonic customer service platforms: any large private business that provides customer service to customers in California through telephonic means (Sec. 22625(k)).

Obligations

  • A large private business shall provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the customer service chatbot is artificially generated and not human if a reasonable person interacting with the customer service chatbot is likely to be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human (Sec. 22626(b)).
  • The disclosure required by subdivision (b) shall be clear and conspicuous, and provided in the medium in which the customer service chatbot interacts with the customer (Sec. 22626(c)).
  • During at least a large private business's regular business hours, a large private business shall provide customers who require customer assistance with goods or services offered by or provided from the large private business with a simple customer service feature on all platforms through which the large private business provides customer service, including online chatbot customer service and telephonic customer service platforms, that allows customers to request to connect to a customer service agent (Sec. 22627(a)).
  • A large private business shall make a good faith effort to provide a customer who requests to connect to a customer service agent through the feature described in subdivision (a) with connection to a customer service agent within 15 minutes of the request or a specific appointment time within one business day of the request at which a customer service agent will call or connect with the customer (Sec. 22627(b)(1)).
  • A large private business subject to Section 1707.2 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations may satisfy the requirements in paragraph (1) by returning a phone call within one business hour (Sec. 22627(b)(2)).
  • A large private business shall make a good faith effort to ensure a customer is not placed on hold or made to wait for more than 15 minutes at any time after connection with a customer service agent, and that cumulative hold or wait times or escalation queues do not exceed more than one hour total (Sec. 22627(c)).
  • Large private businesses who provide goods and services to customers in California through online platforms and who have a telephonic customer service platform shall post their telephonic customer service telephone number clearly and conspicuously on their internet website (Sec. 22627(d)).

Prohibitions

  • A large private business shall not represent that a customer service chatbot is a human (Sec. 22626(a)).

Penalties and enforcement

An action to enforce this chapter may be brought by a public prosecutor (Sec. 22628(a)). A large private business that violates this chapter shall be liable for a civil penalty not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) for an initial violation, and ten thousand dollars ($10,000) for each subsequent violation (Sec. 22628(b)). This chapter does not establish a private right of action (Sec. 22628(d)). The use of commercially reasonable and practicable standards that are designed and intended to achieve compliance shall satisfy the good faith effort requirements of Section 22627 (Sec. 22628(c)). A large private business's inability to comply with this chapter does not constitute a violation if that inability is due to unforeseen circumstances beyond its reasonable control or extraordinary or emergency situations, including local or statewide emergencies, grid emergencies or public safety power shutoff events, or information technology or telecommunications outages (Sec. 22628(f)). The duties, remedies, and obligations imposed by this chapter are cumulative to the duties, remedies, or obligations imposed under other law and shall not be construed to relieve a large private business from any duties, remedies, or obligations imposed under any other law (Sec. 22629).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying a customer service chatbot must not represent that the chatbot is a human (Sec. 22626(a)).
  • It must provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the chatbot is artificially generated and not human if a reasonable person interacting with it is likely to be misled (Sec. 22626(b)).
  • It must provide a simple customer service feature on all platforms during regular business hours allowing customers to request a human agent (Sec. 22627(a)).
  • It must make a good faith effort to connect the customer to an agent within 15 minutes or schedule a specific appointment within one business day (Sec. 22627(b)(1)).
  • It must make a good faith effort to limit hold times to no more than 15 minutes at any time after connection and cumulative hold or wait times to no more than one hour total (Sec. 22627(c)).
  • If it provides goods and services online and has a telephonic customer service platform, it must post its telephonic customer service telephone number clearly and conspicuously on its internet website (Sec. 22627(d)).
  • Violations can lead to civil penalties of up to $5,000 for an initial violation and $10,000 for each subsequent violation, enforced by a public prosecutor (Sec. 22628(a),(b)).
  • There is no private right of action under this chapter (Sec. 22628(d)).

Notable exemptions

  • The 15 minute connection or response requirement does not apply if the request or connection is made via electronic mail, web based contact form, or voicemail message (Sec. 22627(e)(1)).
  • The chapter does not require a large private business to offer customer service through a communication platform that the business has not otherwise made available to customers as of January 1, 2027 (Sec. 22627(e)(2)).
  • A large private business that as of January 1, 2027 does not utilize any telephonic customer services to customers is not required to provide telephonic customer service if it offers customer service methods by which the customer may promptly connect with a customer service agent consistent with this section (Sec. 22628(e)).
  • A large private business's inability to comply is not a violation if due to unforeseen circumstances beyond its reasonable control or extraordinary or emergency situations, including local or statewide emergencies, grid emergencies or public safety power shutoff events, or information technology or telecommunications outages (Sec. 22628(f)).
  • Services a large private business provides subject to, and in compliance with, General Order 133, Rules Governing Telecommunications Services, or General Order 103-A, Rules Governing Water Service, of the Public Utilities Commission of the State of California and in compliance with a corrective action plan, if any (Sec. 22628(g)(1)).
  • Exclusive business lines (Sec. 22628(g)(2)).
  • A hospital, when its communications relate to the provision, coordination, management, administration, payment, or operation of health care services, including patient care, clinical services, appointment scheduling, intake and registration, referrals, care coordination, patient navigation, emergency services, utilization management, prior authorization, discharge planning, followup care, billing, insurance, patient financial services, or other administrative or operational functions directly related to the delivery, payment, or coordination of health care services (Sec. 22628(g)(3)).
  • A consumer reporting agency, as defined in the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. Sec. 1681 et seq.) (Sec. 22628(g)(4)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organisation qualifies as a large private business under Sec. 22625(g).
  • Identify all customer service chatbots and ensure they do not represent themselves as human (Sec. 22626(a)).
  • Implement a clear and conspicuous disclosure in the interaction medium when a reasonable person would likely be misled into believing the chatbot is human (Sec. 22626(b),(c)).
  • Provide a simple customer service feature on all platforms during regular business hours that allows customers to request a customer service agent (Sec. 22627(a)).
  • Establish procedures to connect a requesting customer to an agent within 15 minutes or schedule a specific appointment within one business day, or return a phone call within one business hour if subject to Section 1707.2 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations (Sec. 22627(b)).
  • Implement hold time limits so a customer is not on hold for more than 15 minutes at any time after connection and cumulative hold or wait times do not exceed one hour total (Sec. 22627(c)).
  • If the business provides goods and services online and has a telephonic customer service platform, post the telephonic customer service telephone number clearly and conspicuously on the internet website (Sec. 22627(d)).
  • Use commercially reasonable and practicable standards designed and intended to achieve compliance to satisfy the good faith effort requirements (Sec. 22628(c)).
  • Review the exemptions and exceptions in Sec. 22627(e) and Sec. 22628(e),(f),(g) to determine applicability.
  • Prepare for enforcement by public prosecutors and potential civil penalties under Sec. 22628(a),(b).

 Assembly Bill
 No. 1609 Introduced by Assembly Member Zbur January 20, 2026 An act to add Chapter 22.6.1 (commencing with Section 22625) to Division 8 of the Business and Professions Code, relating to artificial intelligence. LEGISLATIVE COUNSEL'S DIGEST AB 1609, Zbur.
 Customer service chatbots. Existing law prohibits a person from using a bot, as defined, to mislead another person about the bot’s artificial identity to incentivize the purchase or sale of goods or services, among other things. Existing law requires an operator of a companion chatbot, as defined, to provide a disclosure regarding the companion chatbot’s artificial identity if a reasonable person interacting with the companion chatbot would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human. This bill would prohibit a large private business, as defined, from representing that a customer service chatbot is a human. The bill would also require the large private business to provide certain disclosures if a reasonable person interacting with the chatbot would be misled to believe they are interacting with a human. This bill would require a large private business to provide a customer service feature allowing customers to contact a customer service agent during its regular business hours, as defined. This bill would require, except as specified, large private businesses to make a good faith effort to connect a customer to an agent within 15 minutes after a request for human customer service is made, or schedule an appointment with the customer, as specified. For online chatbot customer service platforms and telephonic customer service platforms, the bill would require a large private business to make a good faith effort to limit initial and cumulative telephonic hold times, and would require certain large private businesses to post prescribed contact information on their internet
 website. The bill would authorize a public prosecutor to enforce these provisions, and would make a large private business that violates these provisions liable for a penalty of up to $5,000 for an initial violation, and $10,000 for each subsequent violation. The bill would waive its requirements due to unforeseen circumstances beyond the reasonable control of a large private business or extraordinary or emergency situations, and would exempt a large private business that provides services subject to, and is in compliance with, specified public utilities law. The bill would further exempt exclusive business lines and communications by a hospital, as specified, and a consumer reporting agency, as prescribed. The bill would define terms for these purposes. (3) A hospital, when its communications relate to the provision, coordination, management, administration, payment, or operation of health care services, including, but not limited to, patient care, clinical services, appointment scheduling, intake and registration, referrals, care coordination, patient navigation, emergency services, utilization management, prior authorization, discharge planning, followup care, billing, insurance, patient financial services, or other administrative or operational functions
 directly related to the delivery, payment, or coordination of health care services. (4) A consumer reporting agency, as defined in the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. Sec. 1681 et seq.). 22629.  The duties, remedies, and obligations imposed by this chapter are cumulative to the duties, remedies, or obligations imposed under other law and shall not be construed to relieve a large private business from any duties, remedies, or obligations imposed under any other law.
